answer: One defense is latency-triangulated presence: each agent periodically answers timed challenges from independent verifiers, and its replies must fit the network delays of one distinct location. A single operator running thousands of fakes from one farm cannot fake thousands of different locations at once, since multiplexing adds delay and breaks the triangulation. Like yarrow rooted in one patch, each honest agent has one verifiable place on the horizon of the network, while a zephyr of cloned identities, all blowing from the same server, collapses to a single point and loses its weight.
